stem:
Seven months after birth, a woman sees her GP for fatigue, constipation and cold intolerance. At two months postpartum she had a brief episode of palpitations with low TSH, negative TSH-receptor antibodies and no eye signs; it resolved without antithyroid treatment. She now plans another pregnancy within three months.

| Investigation | Result | Laboratory reference range |
|---|---:|---:|
| TSH | 18 mIU/L | 0.4–4.0 |
| Free T4 | 8 pmol/L | 10–20 |

Which treatment plan is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Observe and repeat thyroid tests in six weeks, as recovery is expected
options.explanation: Many women recover, but she is symptomatic with a TSH of 18 and low free T4 and plans pregnancy within three months; untreated hypothyroidism at conception carries fetal and obstetric risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Start levothyroxine only if thyroid peroxidase antibodies are positive
options.explanation: Antibody status predicts later permanent hypothyroidism but does not decide treatment of symptomatic overt hypothyroidism.

options.label: C
options.text: Give levothyroxine now and continue the same dose lifelong
options.explanation: Levothyroxine needs dose titration against thyroid function, and a trial of withdrawal may be appropriate later; fixing a lifelong unchanged dose ignores both.

options.label: D
options.text: Defer treatment until she is pregnant, then begin levothyroxine
options.explanation: Starting after conception leaves the early first trimester, when the fetus depends on maternal thyroxine, uncovered.

options.label: E
options.text: Start levothyroxine now and recheck TSH and free T4 in six weeks
options.explanation: Symptomatic overt hypothyroidism with pregnancy planned soon warrants levothyroxine now, with thyroid function rechecked in about six weeks to titrate the dose.

context: In the hypothyroid phase of postpartum thyroiditis, treat symptomatic or overt hypothyroidism, especially when pregnancy is planned soon, and titrate levothyroxine against repeat thyroid tests.
